newsitem.title: USA: GM to build low-cost car in Brazil - WSJ.
newsitem.headline: GM to build low-cost car in Brazil - WSJ.

text.p: General Motors Corp is planning to build a new, low-priced small car in Brazil, the Wall Street Journal said.

In Monday's electronic edition, the Journal said the automaker has designed a car that would sell in Brazil for $9,000 or less, which is at least $1,000 less than the next cheapest car sold in that country.
Unnamed sources said the company is hoping to cut the cost of building a car by as much as 25 percent by using outside suppliers more than it has previously.
The hope is to sell cars to new consumers who otherwise would be unable to afford to buy. Global volumes of such a car could exceed one million annually, the Journal said.
"When you think about emerging markets like China, India and Central Europe, at this price point, you could get into that level of volume," said Mark Hogan, GM's director of small-car development.
The Journal said that if plant efficiencies used to make the car in Brazil succeed, GM could bring those same ideas to North America and Europe.
